bib.title: SDEdit: Guided Image Synthesis and Editing with Stochastic Differential Equations
bib.venue: preprint (Under review, ICLR 2022 submission format; arXiv v2 5 Jan 2022)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; figure-only appendix pages (Figs 25-35) have no text beyond captions.

question: How can a pretrained diffusion/SDE generative model do guided image synthesis and editing that balances faithfulness to a user guide and realism, without task-specific training or inversion?
hypothesis: Adding noise to a guide up to an intermediate time t0 and running the reverse SDE projects it onto the natural-image manifold, with t0 controlling a realism-faithfulness trade-off.
contributions: SDEdit: noise the guide to time t0 then run the reverse SDE (training-free, unified for stroke synthesis, stroke editing, compositing)
Analysis of realism-faithfulness trade-off in t0 with a bound (Prop 1)
Human (MTurk) and KID/L2/LPIPS evaluation beating GAN-inversion baselines

method.summary: Take a user guide image, perturb with forward SDE noise to time t0 (x(t0)=x_g+sigma(t0)z for VE), then simulate the reverse SDE to t=0 with a pretrained score model. A mask variant keeps unedited pixels by re-noising the original at each step. Trains nothing.
method.task: guided image synthesis and editing (stroke-to-image, stroke editing, compositing)

datasets.name: LSUN bedroom
datasets.size: 400 generated images per method for human study
datasets.split: validation set for simulated strokes and KID
datasets.preprocessing: stroke simulation: 256x256, median filter kernel 23, reduce to 6 colours via adaptive palette

datasets.name: CelebA-HQ / CelebA 256
datasets.size: 936 composited images (human study); 6000 random CelebA test images for attribute classification

models.name: SDEdit (VP-SDE, LSUN) / (VE-SDE, CelebA-HQ/FFHQ)
models.architecture: pretrained score-based/diffusion models of Song et al. 2021, Ho et al. 2020, Dhariwal & Nichol 2021

models.name: In-domain GAN-1 (encoder only) and GAN-2 (encoder + optimization)

inference.decoding: Euler-Maruyama reverse SDE from t0 to 0 (Algorithms 1-5); optional K repeats of noise+denoise
inference.samples: not stated per item; diverse samples shown per guide

parameters.t0: 0.5 (VP stroke synthesis/editing), 0.45 (VE editing), 0.35 (VE compositing); [0.3,0.6] recommended; 0.6 for coarse cat/horse
parameters.K: 1 (K=1 to 3 works; larger K more realistic but costs more)
parameters.mask: binary Omega; uneditable region set to x0+sigma(t)z each step

metrics.name: L2 (faithfulness)
metrics.definition: L2 distance summed over all pixels between guide and output, images normalised to [0,1]

metrics.name: KID (realism)
metrics.definition: Kernel Inception Distance between generated images and real validation images

metrics.name: MTurk pairwise preference (realism)
metrics.definition: share of workers preferring SDEdit; 'Which image do you think is more realistic'

metrics.name: MTurk pairwise preference (satisfaction)
metrics.definition: guide shown; choose image more reasonable, realistic, less blurry and similar to the input

metrics.name: Masked LPIPS
metrics.definition: LPIPS between edited and unchanged images outside the mask (following Bau et al. 2020)

eval.protocol: MTurk, 15 pairwise questions per HIT, $0.2 per HIT (~$12/h). Stroke realism: 1500 comparisons (100 HITs); stroke satisfaction: 3000 (200 HITs); compositing realism and satisfaction: 1500 each (100 HITs). No significance tests or seeds reported.

prompts.text: Which image do you think is more realistic

Given the input painting, how would you imagine this image to look like in reality? Choose the image that looks more reasonable to you. Your selection should based on how realistic and less blurry the image is, and whether it shares similarities with the input

results.claim: SDEdit beats the GAN baselines on realism by up to 98.09% (MTurk preference) for human-drawn strokes on LSUN bedroom.
results.setup: LSUN bedroom, human-drawn strokes, 400 images/method, 1500 pairwise MTurk comparisons vs StyleGAN2-ADA
results.table: Table 1, row StyleGAN2-ADA, column SDEdit is more realistic

results.claim: SDEdit wins overall satisfaction (realism+faithfulness) by up to 91.72% on human strokes.
results.setup: LSUN bedroom, human strokes, 3000 pairwise MTurk comparisons with the guide shown
results.table: Table 1, row StyleGAN2-ADA, column SDEdit is more satisfactory

results.claim: Closest baseline e4e is still beaten: 80.34% realism and 75.43% satisfaction preference.
results.table: Table 1, row e4e, columns realistic / satisfactory

results.claim: SDEdit has the lowest faithfulness L2 on human strokes (32.55) vs 53.76 for e4e and 101.18 for In-domain GAN-1.
results.setup: LSUN bedroom, human strokes; L2 summed over pixels, images in [0,1]
results.table: Table 1, row SDEdit, column Faithfulness score (L2)

results.claim: On simulated strokes (LSUN bedroom) SDEdit gets KID 0.0030 vs 0.0464 for e4e, and L2 36.76 vs 52.40.
results.setup: LSUN bedroom, algorithm-simulated strokes (6 colours), KID vs validation set
results.table: Table 2, row SDEdit (ours), columns LSUN Bedroom L2 and KID

results.claim: On LSUN church simulated strokes SDEdit gets KID 0.0156 and L2 37.67 vs e4e 0.0354 and 68.53.
results.table: Table 2, row SDEdit (ours), columns LSUN Church L2 and KID

results.claim: Realism-faithfulness trade-off in t0: larger t0 gives more realistic but less faithful outputs; t0 in [0.3, 0.6] is the sweet spot for reasonable guides.
results.setup: LSUN church, simulated stroke guides, KID (realism) and squared L2 to the guide (faithfulness), t0 swept over 0.01 and 0.1..1
results.quote: For reasonable guides, we ﬁnd that t0 ∈[0.3, 0.6] works well.
results.note: t0=0 returns the guide itself, t0=1 a random unconditional sample. Fig 3 caption says 'on LSUN' and App D.2 says LSUN church outdoor; Sec 3 text says 'LSUN dataset'. No numeric KID/L2 values per t0 in text (figure only).

results.claim: Proposition 1 bounds guide deviation: with probability >= 1-delta, ||x_g - SDEdit(x_g;t0)||^2 <= sigma^2(t0)(C sigma^2(t0) + d + 2 sqrt(-d log delta) - 2 log delta), so deviation grows with t0.
results.setup: Assumes score norm squared <= C; d = pixel dimensionality; VE-SDE

results.claim: Default t0 used: 0.5 for stroke synthesis (VP, N=500, K=1) and editing (VP); 0.45 (VE, N=1000) for editing; 0.35 (VE, N=700, K=1) for compositing.
results.setup: Per-task fixed t0 chosen by binary search on one image then shared across the task
results.quote: In this experiment, we use K = 1, N = 500, t0 = 0.5, for SDEdit (VP).

results.claim: Coarser guides need larger t0: t0=0.6 for coarse cat/horse strokes, 0.5 otherwise.
results.setup: LSUN cat and horse, SDEdit VP
results.quote: we choose to slightly sacriﬁce faithfulness in order to obtain more realistic images by selecting a larger t0 = 0.6

results.claim: Image compositing on CelebA-HQ: SDEdit L2 21.70 vs 36.67 (In-domain GAN), 53.90 (e4e), 63.04 (Poisson), 68.45 (Laplacian).
results.setup: CelebA-HQ 256, 936 composited images, SDEdit VE pretrained on FFHQ

results.claim: Compositing overall satisfaction preference for SDEdit up to 83.73% (vs Laplacian blending); realism preference up to 75.60% (vs Poisson).
results.setup: CelebA-HQ compositing, 1500 pairwise comparisons each for realism and satisfaction
results.table: Table 3, row Laplacian Blending, column SDEdit more satisfactory

results.claim: SDEdit is not uniformly more realistic: only 43.67% of workers preferred SDEdit's realism over e4e (i.e. e4e slightly more realistic), and 53.08% vs In-domain GAN.
results.table: Table 3, row e4e, column SDEdit more realistic

results.claim: Masked LPIPS (undesired change outside the mask) is 0.03 for SDEdit vs 0.05 Poisson, 0.09 Laplacian, 0.21 StyleGAN2-ADA, 0.23 In-domain GAN, 0.33 e4e.
SDEdit is tolerant to guide detail: KID 0.0233 (3 colours) to 0.0126 (50 colours) with L2 stable 36.00-37.70, while baselines stay worse.
results.setup: LSUN church, simulated strokes with 3-50 colours

results.claim: Attribute accuracy from simulated strokes on CelebA: SDEdit 0.9232 glasses, 0.8147 gender vs e4e 0.6623 and 0.6175.
results.setup: CelebA 256, 6000 test images, Azure Face API, no face counts as wrong

results.claim: SDEdit takes 29.1s per 256x256 image on one 2080Ti vs 72.8s StyleGAN2-ADA and 5.2s In-domain GAN 2.
results.quote: SDEdit takes 29.1s to generate one image on one 2080Ti GPU.

results.claim: A GAN-fake detector (Wang et al. 2020) detects under 3% of SDEdit LSUN bedroom images vs up to 93% of GAN images.
results.quote: it only successfully detects less than 3% of SDEdit-generated images whereas being able to distinguish up to 93% on GAN-based generation

limits: No numeric KID/L2 values per t0: the trade-off curve is only in Fig 3a; the sweet spot [0.3,0.6] is empirical.
Different guides may have different optimal t0; a shared t0 per task is used and justified only empirically.
Slower than encoder-based GAN inversion (29.1s vs 5.2s); authors suggest faster SDE sampling.
Realism is not uniformly better: e4e preferred over SDEdit for realism on compositing (43.67% prefer SDEdit).
Baselines are GAN inversion methods only; no comparison with conditional GANs trained per task (only qualitative SC-FEGAN).
Needs a pretrained model in the target domain; unconditional, text conditioning not studied (class conditioning via classifier shown in App E.3).
Misuse risk: GAN-fake detector misses SDEdit images; MTurk and user bias may affect metrics.

code.snippet: x <- x + sigma(t0) z; for n=N..1: t=t0*n/N; eps=sqrt(sigma^2(t)-sigma^2(t-dt)); x <- x + eps^2 s_theta(x,t) + eps z
